chapter: Paris, Lester Young, drugs, Mississippi and later sessions
title: Meeting John Lewis through Kenny Clarke
summary: After the war Collins heard John Lewis, whom Kenny Clarke had found in the army, and was impressed by the simplicity and depth of his playing.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: That's right. And I mean, this was just his way. It wasn't -- he wasn't capable of changing. Lester was very strong in his beliefs, and in his life style, you know. So they could destroy him. And something actually happened to him then, you know. So I played with him around New York a couple of times, after that, and he had many groups after that. But to me, I don't know, it was just never -- not quite the same. And incidently, during this -- right after I came out Kenny Clark introduced me to John Lewis. I think Kenny Clark really discovered John Lewis in the army in Europe someplace, I believe. Yeah. So we used to go around to John because John lived on 122nd Street, near 7th Avenue, and I lived on 122nd Street and Morningside, which was not too far. And we would go around to see John. I heard him play, I was very impressed, you know, with the simplicity of his playing, depth. He had a certain something, you know. And after that I played with John, with Dizzy. With Gillespie.
Well, John had that -- before the war John hadn't been in the -- in New York, had he?
Yeah, but I think Kenny persuaded him to come to New York.
He found him in the army.

In the army, yeah,yeah. So I think it was in Europe now, and I think this is what Kenny told me. You know. But this is the first time I met John. Then he went with Dizzy, and from there on, you know --
